q: (Only Allaah knows the correct meaning of these letters.)
v.s: Hā, Meem.
v.c: Ḥâ-Mĩm.

q: By the oath of the Clear Book
v.s: By the clear Book,
v.c: By the clear Book!

q: We have made it an Arabic Qur'aan so that you
(O people of Arabia, who were the first recipients of the Qur'aan)
v.s: Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur’ān that you might understand.
v.c: Certainly, We have made it a Quran in Arabic so perhaps you will understand.

q: Verily, in the Mother Book with Us
v.s: And indeed it is, in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and full of wisdom.
v.c: And indeed, it is—in the Master Record with Us—highly esteemed, rich in wisdom.

q: (However, despite the fact that the Arabs could understand the Qur'aan, many of them refused to accept it. Allaah (therefore asks them,))
(who refuse to accept it)? (Regardless of their refusal to accept the Qur'aan, Allaah still sent the Qur'aan to them so that they cannot claim that they were never shown the path to salvation.)
v.s: Then should We turn the message away, disregarding you, because you are a transgressing people?
v.c: Should We then turn the ˹Quranic˺ Reminder away from you ˹simply˺ because you have been a transgressing people?

q: Numerous were the Ambiyaa that We sent among the former nations
v.s: And how many a prophet We sent among the former peoples,
v.c: ˹Imagine˺ how many prophets We sent to those ˹destroyed˺ before!

q: (However, instead of accepting the message of their Nabi)
every Nabi that came to them.
v.s: But there would not come to them a prophet except that they used to ridicule him.
v.c: But no prophet ever came to them without being mocked.

q: who were much more powerful than these people
The example of the past nations pass
(has been given so that the present nations may learn from their mistakes and not follow them in their awful ways).
v.s: And We destroyed greater than them in [striking] power, and the example of the former peoples has preceded.
v.c: So We destroyed those who were far mightier than these ˹Meccans˺. The examples of ˹their˺ predecessors have ˹already˺ been related.

q: who created the heavens and the earth, they will certainly say, “The Mighty, the All Knowing
v.s: And if you should ask them, "Who has created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "They were created by the Exalted in Might, the Knowing,"
v.c: If you ask them ˹O Prophet˺ who created the heavens and the earth, they will certainly say, “The Almighty, All-Knowing did.”

q: Who made the earth into a bedding
on it for you so that you may be guided
v.s: [The one] who has made for you the earth a bed and made for you upon it roads that you might be guided
v.c: ˹He is the One˺ Who has laid out the earth for you, and set in it pathways for you so that you may find your way.

q: who sends rain from the sky in measure
With this rain We revive dead ground
v.s: And who sends down rain from the sky in measured amounts, and We revive thereby a dead land - thus will you be brought forth -
v.c: And ˹He is the One˺ Who sends down rain from the sky in perfect measure, with which We give life to a lifeless land. And so will you be brought forth ˹from the grave˺.

q: and made ships and animals, which you ride
(when at sea and on land respectively).
v.s: And who created the species, all of them, and has made for you of ships and animals those which you mount
v.c: And ˹He is the One˺ Who created all ˹things in˺ pairs, and made for you ships and animals to ride

q: That you may be seated on their backs and then recall the bounty of your Rabb
when you mount and say, “Pure is Allaah, Who has placed this
at our service whereas we would never have been able to control it
v.s: That you may settle yourselves upon their backs and then remember the favor of your Lord when you have settled upon them and say, "Exalted is He who has subjected this to us, and we could not have [otherwise] subdued it.
v.c: so that you may sit firmly on their backs, and remember your Lord’s blessings once you are settled on them, saying, “Glory be to the One Who has subjected these for us, for we could have never done so ˹on our own˺.

q: “...and our return shall certainly be to our Rabb.”
v.s: And indeed we, to our Lord, will [surely] return."
v.c: And surely to our Lord we will ˹all˺ return.”

q: (However, instead of being grateful to Allaah and worshipping Him Only)
(by saying that they are His children).
v.s: But they have attributed to Him from His servants a portion. Indeed, man is clearly ungrateful.
v.c: Still the pagans have made some of His creation out to be a part of Him. Indeed, humankind is clearly ungrateful.

q: (it become part of their beliefs that)
and selected you to have sons?
(Why would Allaah choose daughters when, according to them, daughters are inferior to sons?)
v.s: Or has He taken, out of what He has created, daughters and chosen you for [having] sons?
v.c: Has He taken ˹angels as His˺ daughters from what He created, and favoured you ˹O pagans˺ with sons?

q: (In fact, they regard having daughters as such a disgrace that)
When any of them is given the tidings of
that which they ascribe to Rahmaan
v.s: And when one of them is given good tidings of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful in comparison [i.e., a daughter], his face becomes dark, and he suppresses grief.
v.c: Whenever one of them is given the good news of what they attribute to the Most Compassionate, his face grows gloomy, as he suppresses his rage.

q: One who is brought up with
and who cannot make herself clear in disputes
v.s: So is one brought up in ornaments while being during conflict unevident [attributed to God]?
v.c: ˹Do they attribute to Him˺ those who are brought up in fineries and are not commanding in disputes?

q: And the angels, who are Allaah's bondsmen, they
(when they say that the angels are Allaah's daughters).
Did they witness the creation of the angels
(that they are so sure of their gender)?
(about this blasphemous statement on the Day of Qiyaamah).
v.s: And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned.
v.c: Still they have labelled the angels, who are servants of the Most Compassionate, as female. Did they witness their creation? Their statement will be recorded, and they will be questioned!

m: we would not have worshipped them
we would not have worshipped them
q: They say, “If Allaah willed, we would not have worshipped
(Whereas Allaah has given them the choice to do good and evil, they shift the blame from themselves by claiming that Allaah has made them commit Shirk.)
v.s: And they said, “If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them.” They have of that no knowledge. They are not but falsifying.
v.c: And they argue, “Had the Most Compassionate willed, we would have never worshipped them.” They have no knowledge ˹in support˺ of this ˹claim˺. They do nothing but lie.

q: (they chosen to remain set in their kufr because they claim that)
v.s: Or have We given them a book before it [i.e., the Qur’ān] to which they are adhering?
v.c: Or have We given them a Book ˹for proof˺, before this ˹Quran˺, to which they are holding firm?

q: They say, “But we found our forefathers following a certain way
and we will be guided in their footsteps.”
v.s: Rather, they say, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and we are in their footsteps [rightly] guided."
v.c: In fact, they say, “We found our forefathers following a ˹particular˺ way, and we are following in their footsteps.”

q: In a like manner, whenever We sent a warner
said, “We found our forefathers following a certain way, and we will be guided in their footsteps.”
v.s: And similarly, We did not send before you any warner into a city except that its affluent said, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and we are, in their footsteps, following."
v.c: Similarly, whenever We sent a warner to a society before you ˹O Prophet˺, its ˹spoiled˺ elite would say, “We found our forefathers following a ˹particular˺ way, and we are walking in their footsteps.”

q: (When faced with this excuse, the Nabi ﷺ replied) “(Will you adhere to the ways of your forefathers)
Even though I have brought to you something that is better guidance than that which you found your forefathers following?”
They replied, “We certainly will not accept what you have been sent with.”
v.s: [Each warner] said, "Even if I brought you better guidance than that [religion] upon which you found your fathers?" They said, "Indeed we, in that with which you were sent, are disbelievers."
v.c: Each ˹warner˺ asked, “Even if what I brought you is better guidance than what you found your forefathers practicing?” They replied, “We totally reject whatever you have been sent with.”

v.s: So We took retribution from them; then see how was the end of the deniers.
v.c: So We inflicted punishment upon them. See then what was the fate of the deniers!

q: When Ibraheem ﵊ said to his father and to his people, “I absolve
v.s: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham said to his father and his people, “Indeed, I am disassociated from that which you worship
v.c: ˹Remember, O Prophet˺ when Abraham declared to his father and his people, “I am totally free of whatever ˹gods˺ you worship,

q: “...except for the One Who has created me
v.s: Except for He who created me; and indeed, He will guide me."
v.c: except the One Who originated me, and He will surely guide me.”

q: as a lasting word among his progeny so that they may abstain
v.s: And he made it a word remaining among his descendants that they might return [to it].
v.c: And he left this enduring declaration among his descendants, so they may ˹always˺ turn back ˹to Allah˺.

q: (but they forgot the message of Ibraheem ﵊ and started committing Shirk)
(when it was time to guide them,)
there came to them the truth
v.s: However, I gave enjoyment to these [people of Makkah] and their fathers until there came to them the truth and a clear Messenger.
v.c: In fact, I had allowed enjoyment for these ˹Meccans˺ and their forefathers, until the truth came to them along with a messenger making things clear.

q: came to them they said, “This is magic
v.s: But when the truth came to them, they said, "This is magic, and indeed we are, concerning it, disbelievers."
v.c: ˹But˺ when the truth came to them, they said, “This is magic, and we totally reject it.”

q: They say, Why is this Qur'aan not revealed to a prominent
man from one of the two cities
(Makkah or Taa'if) “(instead of being revealed to Rasulullaah ﷺ)?
v.s: And they said, "Why was this Qur’ān not sent down upon a great man from [one of] the two cities?"
v.c: And they exclaimed, “If only this Quran was revealed to a great man from ˹one of˺ the two cities!”

q: (Do they have a choice in selecting who Allaah's Rasool should be?) (With regard to worldly matters,)
We distribute their livelihood among them in this worldly life and
the ranks of some of them above others so that they may derive
(by being interdependent). (When this is the state of affairs concerning worldly matters,)
(Prophethood, which is related to the Aakhirah,)
(It is therefore Allaah's right to decide who receives the mantle of Prophethood.)
v.s: Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord? It is We who have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world and have raised some of them above others in degrees [of rank] that they may make use of one another for service. But the mercy of your Lord is better than whatever they accumulate.
v.c: Is it they who distribute your Lord’s mercy? We ˹alone˺ have distributed their ˹very˺ livelihood among them in this worldly life and raised some of them in rank above others so that some may employ others in service. ˹But˺ your Lord’s mercy is far better than whatever ˹wealth˺ they amass.

q: (Whereas the Kuffaar foolishly regard wealth as a token of prominence by which a person becomes eligible for receiving Prophethood, Allaah selects differently. In fact, wealth means nothing to Allah and He could give it in abundance to every Kaafir if it were not foreseeable that everyone would become Kuffaar because of their greed for wealth. Referring to this, Allaah says,)
If it were not for mankind becoming a single nation
(give so much wealth to the Kuffaar that We would)
have made roofs of silver for the homes of those who disbelieve in Rahmaan
v.s: And if it were not that the people would become one community [of disbelievers], We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful - for their houses - ceilings and stairways of silver upon which to mount.
v.c: Were it not that people might ˹be tempted to˺ become one community ˹of disbelievers˺, We would have supplied the homes of ˹only˺ those who disbelieve in the Most Compassionate with silver roofs and ˹silver˺ stairways to ascend,

q: couches on which they may recline.
v.s: And for their houses - doors and couches [of silver] upon which to recline
v.c: as well as ˹silver˺ gates and thrones to recline on,

q: (let alone silver, We could have even made all these things of)
gold. This is all merely the
(which they will surely leave behind them if it does not leave them first). (However,)
v.s: And gold ornament. But all that is not but the enjoyment of worldly life. And the Hereafter with your Lord is for the righteous.
v.c: and ornaments ˹of gold˺. Yet all this is no more than a ˹fleeting˺ enjoyment in this worldly life. ˹But˺ the Hereafter with your Lord is ˹only˺ for those mindful ˹of Him˺.

q: We shall appoint a Shaytaan to
every person who turns a blind eye to Rahmaan's advice
(the Qur'aan and teachings of Rasulullaah ﷺ),
v.s: And whoever is blinded from remembrance of the Most Merciful - We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion.
v.c: And whoever turns a blind eye to the Reminder of the Most Compassionate, We place at the disposal of each a devilish one as their close associate,

q: think that they are rightly guided.
(In this manner, they never have the opportunity to mend their ways because they see no reason to do so.)
v.s: And indeed, they [i.e., the devils] avert them from the way [of guidance] while they think that they are [rightly] guided
v.c: who will certainly hinder them from the ˹Right˺ Way while they think they are ˹rightly˺ guided.

q: (Such a person therefore continues to foolishly follow the directives of this Shaytaan)
Until, when the time arrives for him to come to Us
“O dear! If only there was the distance of the East and West between yourself and Me! A terrible
v.s: Until, when he comes to Us [at Judgement], he says [to his companion], “Oh, I wish there was between me and you the distance between the east and west - how wretched a companion.”
v.c: But when such a person comes to Us, one will say ˹to their associate˺, “I wish you were as distant from me as the east is from the west! What an evil associate ˹you were˺!”

q: (It will then be said to all of them)
the fact that you all share the punishment shall be of no benefit to you.”
(Neither will any of you be able to take solace from the fact that others are suffering the same fate, nor will you be able to help each other.)
v.s: And never will it benefit you that Day, when you have wronged, that you are [all] sharing in the punishment.
v.c: ˹It will be said to both,˺ “Since you all did wrong, sharing in the punishment will be of no benefit to you this Day.”

q: (those who refuse to see the truth)
and those who are in manifest deviation
(clearly in the wrong)? (Such people refuse to accept guidance and you cannot force them to do so. Therefore, do not grieve over them.)
v.s: Then will you make the deaf hear, [O Muhammad], or guide the blind or he who is in clear error?
v.c: Can you make the deaf hear, or guide the blind or those clearly astray?

q: If We have to take you away
(punish them after your demise or in the Aakhirah).
v.s: And whether [or not] We take you away [in death], indeed, We will take retribution upon them.
v.c: Even if We take you away ˹from this world˺, We will surely inflict punishment upon them.

q: We have promised them, for We certainly have control
(and can punish them whenever We wish).
v.s: Or whether [or not] We show you that which We have promised them, indeed, We are Perfect in Ability.
v.c: Or if We show you what We threaten them with, We certainly have full power over them.

q: ('do not worry about them, but rather)
hold fast to the revelation We have sent
to you. You are definitely upon the straight path
(and the opposition of the Kuffaar will not change this fact).
v.s: So adhere to that which is revealed to you. Indeed, you are on a straight path.
v.c: So hold firmly to what has been revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺. You are truly on the Straight Path.

q: and for your people. Soon, they shall be questioned
(about whether they practised its teachings and propagated them).
v.s: And indeed, it is a remembrance for you and your people, and you [all] are going to be questioned.
v.c: Surely this ˹Quran˺ is a glory for you and your people. And you will ˹all˺ be questioned ˹about it˺.

q: Inquire from those Rusul of Ours whom We have sent before you
(by referring to their teachings. Ask them)
Have We introduced other Aaliha who can be worshipped Besides Rahmaan?
(The teachings of every Nabi ﷺ emphasised that Only Allaah should be worshipped.)
v.s: And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers; have We made besides the Most Merciful deities to be worshipped?
v.c: Ask ˹the followers of˺ the messengers that We already sent before you if We ˹ever˺ appointed ˹other˺ gods to be worshipped besides the Most Compassionate.

q: Undoubtedly, We sent Moosa ﵊ with Our Aayaat
said, “I am the Rasool of the Rabb of the universe.”
v.s: And certainly did We send Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his establishment, and he said, "Indeed, I am the messenger of the Lord of the worlds."
v.c: Indeed, We sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, and he said: “I am a messenger of the Lord of all worlds.”

q: When he came to them with Our Aayaat
v.s: But when he brought them Our signs, at once they laughed at them.
v.c: But as soon as he came to them with Our signs, they laughed at them,

q: We showed them was greater than the other.
v.s: And We showed them not a sign except that it was greater than its sister, and We seized them with affliction that perhaps they might return [to faith].
v.c: although every sign We showed them was greater than the one before. Ultimately, We seized them with torments so that they might return ˹to the Right Path˺.

q: (used as a title of honour in those days)!
On our behalf, pray to your Rabb for the covenant He has made with you
(that He would remove the punishment if we accept Imaan).
we will surely be rightly guided.”
v.s: And they said [to Moses], "O magician, invoke for us your Lord by what He has promised you. Indeed, we will be guided."
v.c: ˹Then˺ they pleaded, “O ˹mighty˺ magician! Pray to your Lord on our behalf, by virtue of the covenant He made with you. We will certainly accept guidance.”

q: from them, they immediately broke their promise
v.s: But when We removed from them the affliction, at once they broke their word.
v.c: But as soon as We removed the torments from them, they broke their promise.

q: Fir'oun called his people saying, “Does not the land
of Egypt and these rivers flowing beneath belong to me? Do you not see
(that you should rather be listening to me instead of Moosa)
v.s: And Pharaoh called out among his people; he said, "O my people, does not the kingdom of Egypt belong to me, and these rivers flowing beneath me; then do you not see?
v.c: And Pharaoh called out to his people, boasting, “O my people! Am I not sovereign over Egypt as well as ˹all˺ these streams flowing at my feet? Can you not see?

q: “Am I not better than this person
v.s: Or am I [not] better than this one [i.e., Moses] who is insignificant and hardly makes himself clear?
v.c: Am I not better than this nobody who can hardly express himself?

q: Why are bangles of gold not thrown
(why does he not have wealth, I were gold bangles),
or why do angels not follow him in procession
v.s: Then why have there not been placed upon him bracelets of gold or come with him the angels in conjunction?"
v.c: Why then have no golden bracelets ˹of kingship˺ been granted to him or angels come with him as escorts!”

q: (by convincing them to follow him instead of Moosa ﵊)
and they followed him. They were a sinful
v.s: So he bluffed his people, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were [themselves] a people defiantly disobedient [of God].
v.c: And so he fooled his people, and they obeyed him. They were truly a rebellious people.

q: (by persisting with Shirk and harassing the Mu'mineen)
retribution from them and drowned them all
v.s: And when they angered Us, We took retribution from them and drowned them all.
v.c: So when they enraged Us, We inflicted punishment upon them, drowning them all.

q: (from whose bitter experience later generations were to learn)
and an example for those to come after them.
v.s: And We made them a precedent and an example for the later peoples.
v.c: And We made them an example and a lesson for those after them.

q: When the unique example of the son of Maryam

(when you tell the Mushrikeen that there is no benefit in all the gods that they worship, someone of them say that there is therefore no good in worshipping Isa ﵊ as well, whom some Christians worship,)
v.s: And when the son of Mary was presented as an example, immediately your people laughed aloud.
v.c: When the son of Mary was cited as an example ˹in argument˺, your people ˹O Prophet˺ broke into ˹joyful˺ applause.
v.h: All Objects of Worship in Hell?

q: They say this to you only to dispute, for they are a people given to arguing.
(They realise that it is their idols that are being referred to, but merely raise the objection to develop an argument.)
v.s: And they said, “Are your gods better, or is he?” They did not present it [i.e., the comparison] except for [mere] argument. But, [in fact], they are a people prone to dispute.
v.c: They exclaimed, “Which is better: our gods or Jesus?” They cite him only to argue. In fact, they are a people prone to dispute.

q: and whom We have made an example for the Bani Israa'eel
(and for mankind after them to prove to them that Allaah can create without the obvious means of a father).
v.s: He [i.e., Jesus] was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel.
v.c: He was only a servant We showed favour to, and made as an example for the Children of Israel.

q: (In fact, Allaah's power is limitless because)
If We willed, We could have created angels among you
on earth, who would appear in
v.s: And if We willed, We could have made [instead] of you angels succeeding [one another] on the earth.
v.c: Had We willed, We could have easily replaced you ˹all˺ with angels, succeeding one another on earth.

q: is certainly a sign of Qiyaamah
(proving that just as Allaah created him miraculously, Allaah can also enact the miraculous feat of resurrecting mankind),
so never doubt it, and follow me.
v.s: And indeed, he [i.e., Jesus] will be [a sign for] knowledge of the Hour, so be not in doubt of it, and follow Me. This is a straight path.
v.c: And his ˹second˺ coming is truly a sign for the Hour. So have no doubt about it, and follow me. This is the Straight Path.

q: for he is certainly your open
(and will do everything to stop you).
v.s: And never let Satan avert you. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
v.c: And do not let Satan hinder you, ˹for˺ he is certainly your sworn enemy.

q: When Isa ﵊ came with the clear signs
(to prove Towheed and the fact that he was Allaah's Nabi),
he said, “I have come to you with wisdom
and to make clear to you the matters about which you quarrel. So fear Allaah and follow me.”
v.s: And when Jesus brought clear proofs, he said, "I have come to you with wisdom [i.e., prophethood] and to make clear to you some of that over which you differ, so fear God and obey me.
v.c: When Jesus came with clear proofs, he declared, “I have come to you with wisdom, and to clarify to you some of what you differ about. So fear Allah, and obey me.

q: “Allaah is definitely my Rabb and your Rabb, so worship Him only. This
v.s: Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path."
v.c: Surely Allah ˹alone˺ is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him ˹alone˺. This is the Straight Path.”

v.s: But the denominations from among them differed [and separated], so woe to those who have wronged from the punishment of a painful Day.
v.c: Yet their ˹various˺ groups have differed among themselves ˹about him˺, so woe to the wrongdoers when they face the torment of a painful Day!

q: for Qiyaamah to come to them suddenly without them realising
(However, it will then be too late.)
v.s: Are they waiting except for the Hour to come upon them suddenly while they perceive not?
v.c: Are they waiting for the Hour to take them by surprise when they least expect ˹it˺?

q: Friends will be enemies on that day
(of Qiyaamah because they will refuse to assist each other),
(who will remain loyal to each other).
v.s: Close friends, that Day, will be enemies to each other, except for the righteous
v.c: Close friends will be enemies to one another on that Day, except the righteous,

q: (Allaah will say to the people of Taqwa on the Day of Qiyaamah,)
v.s: [To whom God will say], "O My servants, no fear will there be concerning you this Day, nor will you grieve,
v.c: ˹who will be told,˺ “O My servants! There is no fear for you Today, nor will you grieve—

q: Those who believed in Our Aayaat and were
v.s: [You] who believed in Our verses and were Muslims.
v.c: ˹those˺ who believed in Our signs and ˹fully˺ submitted ˹to Us˺.

q: “You and your spouses should enter into Jannah happily
v.s: Enter Paradise, you and your kinds, delighted."
v.c: Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, rejoicing.”

q: will be passed around between them and in Jannah there shall be whatever the heart desires and whatever pleases the eye
(the greatest bounty being the ability to see Allaah).
v.s: Circulated among them will be plates and vessels of gold. And therein is whatever the souls desire and [what] delights the eyes, and you will abide therein eternally.
v.c: Golden trays and cups will be passed around to them. There will be whatever the souls desire and the eyes delight in. And you will be there forever.

q: “This is Jannah, which you have been made to inherit because of the
v.s: And that is Paradise which you are made to inherit for what you used to do.
v.c: That is the Paradise which you will be awarded for what you used to do.

q: you will have an abundance of fruit
(there shall never be any shortage there).”
v.s: For you therein is much fruit from which you will eat.
v.c: There you will have abundant fruit to eat from.

q: shall suffer the punishment of Jahannam forever.
v.s: Indeed, the criminals will be in the punishment of Hell, abiding eternally.
v.c: Indeed, the wicked will be in the torment of Hell forever.

q: The punishment shall not be reduced for them, and they will lose all hope
v.s: It will not be allowed to subside for them, and they, therein, are in despair.
v.c: It will never be lightened for them, and there they will be overwhelmed with despair.

q: (their punishment is the result of the sins that they committed despite the advice and warnings We sent to them).
v.s: And We did not wrong them, but it was they who were the wrongdoers.
v.c: We did not wrong them, but it was they who were the wrongdoers.

q: (quickly to allow us to die instead of suffering here eternally).”
will reply, “You people will certainly have to remain
v.s: And they will call, "O Mālik, let your Lord put an end to us!" He will say, "Indeed, you will remain."
v.c: They will cry, “O Mâlik! Let your Lord finish us off.” He will answer, “You are definitely here to stay.”

q: “We definitely brought the truth to you, but most of you disliked
(and therefore you have to suffer punishment here).'
v.s: We had certainly brought you the truth, but most of you, to the truth, were averse.
v.c: We certainly brought the truth to you, but most of you were resentful of the truth.

q: (besides having a dislike for the truth)
(to protect Rasulullaah ﷺ and punish them- and Our plan always prevails over all others).
v.s: Or have they devised [some] affair? But indeed, We are devising [a plan].
v.c: Or have they mastered some ˹evil˺ plan? Then We ˹too˺ are surely planning.

q: (they plot against Islaam and the Muslims because)
they think that We do not hear their secrets and their stealthy meetings
and Our scribes are with them
v.s: Or do they think that We hear not their secrets and their private conversations? Yes, [We do], and Our messengers [i.e., angels] are with them recording.
v.c: Or do they think that We do not hear their ˹evil˺ thoughts and secret talks? Yes ˹We do˺! And Our messenger-angels are in their presence, recording ˹it all˺.

q: “If Rahmaan had a son, then I would have been the first to worship
(His children).” (However, because I am convinced that He has no children, I worship Allaah Alone.)
v.s: Say, [O Muhammad], “If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of [his] worshippers.”
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “If the Most Compassionate ˹really˺ had offspring, I would be the first worshipper.”

q: The Rabb of the heavens and the earth, the Rabb of the Throne is Pure from whatever
v.s: Exalted is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.
v.c: Glorified is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, far above what they claim.

q: (after conveying the message of Islaam to the Kuffaar)
v.s: So leave them to converse vainly and amuse themselves until they meet their Day which they are promised.
v.c: So let them indulge ˹in falsehood˺ and amuse ˹themselves˺ until they face their Day, which they have been warned of.

q: It is Allaah Who is the Ilaah in the heavens and the Ilaah on earth. He is the Wise, the All Knowing.
v.s: And it is He [i.e., God] who is [the only] deity in the heaven, and on the earth [the only] deity. And He is the Wise, the Knowing.
v.c: It is He Who is ˹the only˺ God in the heavens and ˹the only˺ God on the earth. For He is the All-Wise, All-Knowing.
v.h: The Only God Worthy of Worship

q: Blessed is that Being to Whom belongs the kingdom of the heavens, the earth and whatever is between the two. The knowledge of Qiyaamah is only with Him, and to Him shall you all be returned
v.s: And blessed is He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them and with whom is knowledge of the Hour and to whom you will be returned.
v.c: And Blessed is the One to Whom belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and everything in between! With Him ˹alone˺ is the knowledge of the Hour. And to Him you will ˹all˺ be returned.

q: worship besides Allaah have no power to intercede, except
for the one who attests to
(who are convinced about the truth of Towheed).
v.s: And those they invoke besides Him do not possess [power of] intercession; but only those who testify to the truth [can benefit], and they know.
v.c: ˹But˺ those ˹objects of worship˺ they invoke besides Him have no power to intercede, except those who testify to the truth knowingly.
v.h: Call to the Worshippers of False Gods

q: If you have to ask them
who created them, they will definitely say, “Allaah”.
v.s: And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "God." So how are they deluded?
v.c: If you ask them ˹O Prophet˺ who created them, they will certainly say, “Allah!” How can they then be deluded ˹from the truth˺?

q: statement when he said, “O my Rabb! This is a nation who refuse to accept Imaan
(despite being given every opportunity to do so).”
v.s: And [God acknowledges] his saying, "O my Lord, indeed these are a people who do not believe."
v.c: ˹Allah is Aware of˺ the Prophet’s cry: “O my Lord! Indeed, these are a people who persist in disbelief.”

q: (do not entertain any hopes of them ever accepting Imaan and so do not be disappointed)
They will soon come to know
(the error of their ways in the Aakhirah if not sooner).
v.s: So turn aside from them and say, "Peace." But they are going to know.
v.c: So bear with them and respond with peace. They will soon come to know.
